description:
Analyze the user's stock portfolio.

    Returns concentration risk (low/medium/high), a diversification
    score (0-10), a sector breakdown (looking through known ETFs), the
    biggest winner and loser by dollar impact, and a short written
    summary. Use this when the user asks how diversified, concentrated or
    risky their portfolio is. Don't use it just to list holdings (use
    list_portfolio).

    Limits: requires sign-in. Prices can be up to 7 days old; positions
    without a price are labeled, never guessed.
    Educational information, not investment advice.
name: analyze_portfolio

HoldingSummary.description:
One-line reference to a holding by ticker + its P&L. Used to
reference biggest_winner / biggest_loser without inlining the
full Position (which would drift from list_portfolio's output).

BUG-41 (2026-08-24): added `pnl_dollars` alongside `pnl_pct` so
LLM narrators can quote BOTH numbers verbatim without recomputing
(LLM Scope Boundary). Winner/loser ranking is now by absolute
dollar impact, not percentage — a $87 loss on a $3 position that
started at $91 is a meaningful portfolio event; a +36% gain on
a $5 position is not.
HoldingSummary.title: HoldingSummary

outputSchema.description:
Return type for `analyze_portfolio()`. LLM-narrated PhD-style
analysis over the caller's merged holdings.

LLM Scope Boundary compliance (CLAUDE.md): every numeric field
(diversification_score, sector_breakdown, pnl_pct) is computed
in Python BEFORE the LLM sees it. The `summary` narrative is the
ONLY LLM-produced text — and its prompt uses `_format_named_fields`
with a TRUST_RULE that the LLM must reference field names
verbatim, never recompute.

Post-BUG-24: `is_empty=True` with `upgrade_hint` for anon /
empty-tenant callers. Never fake analysis.
outputSchema.title: PortfolioAnalysis

title: Analyze My Portfolio
